Exercise 15.7.55 — Maximizing a Triple Integral over a Region

Problem. (a) Find the region EEE for which the triple integral ∭E(1−x2−2y2−3z2) dV \iiint_E (1 - x^2 - 2y^2 - 3z^2)\, dV ∭E​(1−x2−2y2−3z2)dV is a maximum. (b) Use a computer algebra system to calculate the exact maximum value of the triple integral in (a).

Part 1 — The maximizing region

Step 1.1: Sign of the integrand.

Write g(x,y,z)=1−x2−2y2−3z2g(x,y,z) = 1 - x^2 - 2y^2 - 3z^2g(x,y,z)=1−x2−2y2−3z2. Then g≥0g \ge 0g≥0 exactly on the ellipsoid E0={(x,y,z):x2+2y2+3z2≤1}, E_0 = \{(x,y,z): x^2 + 2y^2 + 3z^2 \le 1\}, E0​={(x,y,z):x2+2y2+3z2≤1}, and g<0g < 0g<0 everywhere outside it. The script solution/part1_step1.py verifies this sign pattern at eight sample points (four inside E0E_0E0​, four outside), each by exact rational arithmetic.

Step 1.2: Why E0 is the maximizer.

Suppose a region EEE omits a set AAA of positive volume on which g>0g > 0g>0. Then F(E∪A)−F(E)=∭Ag dV>0, F(E \cup A) - F(E) = \iiint_A g\, dV > 0, F(E∪A)−F(E)=∭A​gdV>0, so FFF increases. Likewise, if EEE contains a set of positive volume on which g<0g < 0g<0, deleting it increases FFF. Hence a maximum can only be attained by a region that contains all points with g>0g > 0g>0 and no points with g<0g < 0g<0; the maximizing region is therefore exactly E=E0={(x,y,z):x2+2y2+3z2≤1}. E = E_0 = \{(x,y,z): x^2 + 2y^2 + 3z^2 \le 1\}. E=E0​={(x,y,z):x2+2y2+3z2≤1}.

As a check, the same script computes Vol(E0)\text{Vol}(E_0)Vol(E0​) in three ways: the semi-axis formula 43πabc\tfrac{4}{3}\pi abc34​πabc, the change of variables (x,y,z)=(u,v/2,w/3)(x,y,z) = (u, v/\sqrt{2}, w/\sqrt{3})(x,y,z)=(u,v/2​,w/3​) (Jacobian 1/61/\sqrt{6}1/6​) applied to the exact volume of the unit ball, and a Monte-Carlo estimate. All agree: Vol(E0)=26 π9≈1.7100664. \text{Vol}(E_0) = \frac{2\sqrt{6}\,\pi}{9} \approx 1.7100664. Vol(E0​)=926​π​≈1.7100664.

Result (a). The maximizing region is the ellipsoid E={(x,y,z):x2+2y2+3z2≤1}. E = \{(x,y,z): x^2 + 2y^2 + 3z^2 \le 1\}. E={(x,y,z):x2+2y2+3z2≤1}.
